classification.classification_note: The saved ASan crash is the read-side manifestation of the broader Content-Length parsing bug: the shared parse-error logger dereferences `*p` after the parser has already advanced to end-of-input.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in core where the parsing of the Content-Length header does not properly consider the multi-line header format. Additionally, there are missing safety checks for log messages when the message buffer is not being parsed.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized:
The staged 17-byte witness ends with `
L:3 `, where compact SIP header name `L` maps to Content-Length. `get_hdr_field()` recognizes that compact header and, after trimming post-colon LWS, passes the bounded body span `3 ` at the end of the heap-backed libFuzzer input to `parse_content_length()`. Vulnerable `parse_content_length()` parses digit `3`, then its trailing-whitespace loop consumes the final space and leaves `p == end` because the input ends immediately after that space, with no `
`, `
`, or continuation line. The function then takes the shared `error:` path and unconditionally formats `*p` in `LM_ERR("parse error near char [%d][%c]
", *p, *p);`, dereferencing one byte past the 17-byte heap buffer. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/core/parser/parse_content.c:251` with stack `parse_content_length -> get_hdr_field -> parse_headers`. Fix commit `baed515e8aed8e5b505ff716eb57d0c60e582632` closes this exact unsafe state by guarding the EOF log with `if(p<end)` / `else`, and in the same hunk rewrites the end-of-header loop to handle multiline Content-Length bodies and end-of-buffer cases explicitly. Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

source.description: First project-side parser step that consumes attacker-controlled header bytes and materializes the dispatch key for the vulnerable Content-Length path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 17 bytes: `ff ff 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 0a 4c 3a 33 20`. On the crashing header line, the suffix bytes `4c 3a 33 20` are `L:3 `. `parse_hname2()` matches compact header name `l`/`L` to `HDR_CONTENTLENGTH_T` and returns `tmp` just after the colon.

sink.description: ASan crash site. With `p == end`, the first `*p` in this log call performs a 1-byte read at the first byte past the 17-byte heap-backed fuzz input.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1` at `src/core/parser/parse_content.c:251:2`, with `get_hdr_field`, `parse_headers`, and `parse_msg` immediately below it.

root_cause.description: Missing EOF guard on the shared parse-error logger. After the parser has already advanced `p` to `end`, this log call still dereferences `*p`. The patch fixes the exact obligation by testing `if(p<end)` before formatting `*p` and emitting a separate over-end message otherwise.
root_cause.note: On the staged witness, the preceding trailing-whitespace logic reaches `p == end` because the compact `L:3 ` header ends immediately after the space. This line is therefore both the root cause and the concrete out-of-bounds read site.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes the exact bounded Content-Length body span that drives the bug. For the witness suffix `L:3 `, it leaves `tmp` on digit `'3'` and keeps `end` one byte past the final space, so the later whitespace-skip can advance precisely to `end`.

parser_admitted.description: Header dispatch has already selected `HDR_CONTENTLENGTH_T`, so this call enters the vulnerable Content-Length parser on the bounded body span beginning at `'3'`. The saved ASan stack confirms this exact `get_hdr_field -> parse_content_length` transition.

coarse_trace.summary: The header parser recognizes the witness suffix `L:` as compact Content-Length, trims post-colon LWS, and enters `parse_content_length()` on the final two bytes `3 `.
`parse_content_length()` parses digit `3`, then its trailing-whitespace loop consumes the last in-bounds space byte and leaves `p == end` because no header terminator follows.
The shared error logger still formats `*p` after EOF, so the saved AddressSanitizer trace reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at line 251.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing header line, this call consumes the bytes `L:` from the witness suffix `\nL:3 ` and, via `parse_hname2`, maps compact header name `L` to `HDR_CONTENTLENGTH_T`. The returned `tmp` points just after the colon, establishing the Content-Length dispatch key used by the later switch.

With no whitespace between the colon and the body in `L:3 `, `eat_lws_end` leaves `tmp` at the digit `'3'`. The remaining bounded span for Content-Length parsing is therefore the final two input bytes `3 `, with `end` still at the first byte past the 17-byte buffer.

In the `HDR_CONTENTLENGTH_T` case, `parse_content_length()` parses the single body digit `'3'`. After one loop iteration, `number == 3`, `size == 1`, and `p` has advanced from the digit to the trailing space byte.
On this witness the only remaining in-bounds byte is the trailing space after `3`, so this loop executes once through its `*p == ' '` arm and advances `p` from the last valid byte to `end`.

Because the input ends immediately after that trailing space, there is no `\n`, `\r\n`, or continuation line for a header terminator. The function therefore reaches the shared error path with `p == end`.

Root cause and sink. The error logger unconditionally formats `*p` even though step 5 has already established `p == end`. That first dereference reads one byte past the 17-byte heap input, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `src/core/parser/parse_content.c:251`. The patch fixes this exact line by guarding the log with `if(p<end)` and using a separate EOF message otherwise.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of the 17-byte heap buffer allocated for the current libFuzzer testcase.
